claims.claim: Snowflake's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 discloses that its amended third-party AI service-provider agreement increased the three-year minimum purchase commitment to $390 million, with $270 million remaining as of July 31, 2026.

The same filing discloses a $6.0 billion cumulative minimum-spend commitment under an amended third-party cloud infrastructure agreement through March 31, 2031, with annual minimums ranging from $900 million to $1.25 billion.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Large multi-year AI-service and cloud-infrastructure commitments secure capacity access but create material fixed purchase obligations if consumption or workload economics underperform.

factors.name: crossDivisionLeverage
factors.basis: Committed AI-service and cloud capacity can support expansion of Snowflake's AI workloads across the platform, while dependence on third-party infrastructure/providers remains economically material.

risks.risk: Minimum-spend commitments can pressure economics if realized AI or cloud consumption falls below contracted levels.
Material reliance on third-party AI services and cloud infrastructure limits full-stack control over cost and capacity economics.

unknowns.unknown: The filing does not isolate revenue or gross margin attributable specifically to workloads supported by these commitments.
